title: Neighbor Love and Mercy
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Neighbor love and mercy means moving toward people in need with compassion, sacrifice, and practical help. Love for neighbor is not limited to people who are familiar, convenient, similar, or able to repay.
summary: Neighbor love and mercy means moving toward people in need with compassion, sacrifice, and practical help. Love for neighbor is not limited to people who are familiar, convenient, similar, or able to repay.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the merciful Savior who moved toward sinners in their need. His compassion teaches His people to love others with action, cost, and mercy.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Jesus taught neighbor love through the parable of the Samaritan. The neighbor was the one who showed mercy, crossing barriers and paying a cost to help the wounded man.

Mercy is practical. It sees need, moves toward it, and acts. Scripture does not allow love to remain only words when a brother or sister lacks what is needed.

Neighbor love is broad. Believers are called to do good to all, especially to those of the household of faith. Love cannot be limited to people who are easy to love.

Mercy reflects God’s own character. The Lord delights in mercy, justice, and humble walking before Him. His people should display those realities in daily relationships.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People in need are often passed by because others are busy, afraid, prejudiced, or self-protective. Neighbor love interrupts self-centered living.

This doctrine helps believers ask not only, “Who is my neighbor?” but “How can I become a neighbor to the person God has placed before me?”

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Move toward need with mercy. Look for practical ways to help the wounded, burdened, lonely, poor, or overlooked. Love with action, not merely intention, and remember that Christ showed mercy to you when you could not save yourself.
